skill.name: github-code-review
skill.description: AI-assisted GitHub pull request review workflow using GitHub CLI, ruv-swarm examples, and coordinated review agents.
skill.summary: Coordinate AI-assisted reviews for GitHub pull requests across security, performance, style, and architecture checks.
skill.author: Claude Code Flow

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick detections are false positives from Markdown code fences and inline formatting. Real risks remain in the webhook example that executes PR comment text, use of runtime npx commands, and handling of GitHub tokens for repository mutations.

remediation.issue: Webhook command execution from PR comments
remediation.suggestion: Verify GitHub webhook signatures, parse request bodies safely, allowlist commands, and replace execSync shell strings with argument-array execution.

remediation.issue: Runtime execution of external packages with npx
remediation.suggestion: Pin ruv-swarm versions, install through a locked dependency manifest, and run review commands only in controlled CI environments.

remediation.issue: GitHub token use in automated workflows
remediation.suggestion: Set explicit least-privilege workflow permissions, pass tokens through GH_TOKEN or scoped credentials, and avoid echoing secrets into command pipelines.
Require protected branch checks, human approval, and structured trusted status signals before approving or merging pull requests.

static_findings.snippet: run: echo "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" | gh auth login --with-token

finding_verdicts.reason: The webhook example imports child_process and the same block executes shell commands from webhook events. This is dangerous if copied without strict validation and isolation.
execSync runs a shell command inside a webhook handler using event data. The PR number is expected numeric, but synchronous shell execution in a webhook remains high impact.
execSync interpolates a PR comment body into a shell command. PR comments are user-controlled, so this is command injection unless strictly authenticated and allowlisted.

semantic_findings.title: Webhook Executes Untrusted PR Comments
semantic_findings.description: The webhook example accepts PR comments starting with /swarm and passes the full comment body into a shell command. The surrounding handler does not show GitHub signature verification, an allowlist, or safe argument execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code reads event.comment.body and interpolates it into execSync. PR comments are attacker-controlled in many repository workflows unless separately authenticated and allowlisted.

semantic_findings.title: Automated PR Approval and Merge Logic
semantic_findings.description: The workflow examples approve a pull request when review output contains the word approved, and later enable auto-merge based on swarm status and review count. This can create unsafe business logic if tool output is influenced or branch protection is weak.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples contain concrete gh pr review --approve and gh pr merge --auto commands controlled by parsed text or status checks. The pattern is legitimate automation but needs stronger policy gates.

content.user_title: Review GitHub Pull Requests with AI Swarms
content.value_statement: Large pull requests are hard to review consistently across security, performance, and architecture concerns. This skill provides GitHub CLI and swarm-based workflows for coordinated AI-assisted review.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to collect pull request metadata and diffs with GitHub CLI.
Defines security, performance, architecture, style, and accessibility review agent examples.
Provides GitHub Actions examples for automated review workflows.
Demonstrates inline review comment generation and posting through GitHub APIs.
Describes quality gates, review metrics, progress updates, and troubleshooting steps.
Includes guidance for token scope, command validation, rate limits, and audit logs.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI, ruv-swarm, claude-flow, and repository authentication to be configured.
Several examples execute external commands and should only run in trusted environments.
Automated approval and merge examples need human guardrails before production use.
Review results depend on configured agents and do not replace maintainer judgment.

use_cases.title: Coordinate PR Reviews
use_cases.description: Run structured reviews that split security, performance, style, and architecture checks across specialized agents.

use_cases.title: Add Security Review Gates
use_cases.description: Create review flows that flag critical security issues and request changes before a pull request can merge.

use_cases.title: Automate Review Workflows
use_cases.description: Build GitHub Actions workflows that collect PR context, run review agents, post summaries, and update labels.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Pull Request Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pull request 123. Summarize the main changes, list the highest priority issues, and suggest next review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Focused Security Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pull request 123 for authentication, authorization, secret exposure, and input validation risks. Prioritize findings by impact.

prompt_templates.title: CI Review Workflow Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Design a repeatable GitHub Actions review workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an automated review workflow for pull requests. Include required agents, quality gates, labels, and safe token handling.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Multi-Agent Review Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a coordinated review for a large or high-risk pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multi-agent review plan for pull request 123. Assign agents, define review depth, set escalation rules, and specify merge criteria.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request that changes authentication code.
output: Security review requested changes for missing authorization checks.
Architecture review found no blocking design issues.
Recommended next step: add tests for denied access paths before approval.

output_examples.input: Create an automated review flow for a large feature branch.
output: The workflow collects pull request context, runs focused review agents, posts a summary, and labels follow-up areas.
Human approval remains required before merge.

output_examples.input: Generate review comments for performance-sensitive database changes.
output: Performance feedback highlights query count, caching behavior, and baseline comparison needs.
Comments are grouped by severity so maintainers can address blocking items first.

best_practices: Run examples only in repositories where GitHub tokens and branch permissions are tightly scoped.
Pin external tool versions and review package provenance before using npx-based commands.
Require human approval for merge, approval, and label changes in protected branches.
anti_patterns: Do not execute pull request comments as shell commands without signature checks and allowlists.
Do not grant broad repository tokens to automated review workflows.
Do not approve or merge pull requests based only on unstructured tool output.

faq.question: Does this skill review GitHub pull requests directly?
faq.answer: It provides workflows and command examples for AI-assisted GitHub pull request review. The required tools must be configured separately.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: The skill expects GitHub CLI, ruv-swarm, claude-flow, and an authenticated repository environment.

faq.question: Can it post review comments?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show how to generate comments and post inline pull request feedback through GitHub APIs.

faq.question: Is it safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: Automatic use needs guardrails. Limit token permissions, validate webhook input, and require human approval for merge actions.

faq.question: Does it replace human reviewers?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize review coverage, but maintainers should verify findings and approve final changes.

faq.question: Can Codex, Claude, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, with examples centered on GitHub workflows.
